facts.raw_span: multiple swellings of five months’ duration
progressive enlargement of bilateral neck masses and one each on her back and anterior abdominal wall, without pain
no significant past medical, personal, or family history
seven subcutaneous, nontender, mobile swellings measuring 1×1 to 3×3 cm in the cervical regions, right paraspinal area, and anterior abdominal wall
the lesions were firm to hard without changes in the overlying skin
Complete blood count, metabolic panel, and skeletal survey were all normal
cytology smears from all sites showed moderate cellularity with similar features: predominantly plump spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm
nuclear hyperchromasia, pleomorphism, or atypicality was not seen, and mitoses were sparse
there was no necrosis or inflammatory cells
Ultrasonography confirmed that all lesions were confined to the subcutaneous tissue, with no lymphadenopathy or deeper masses
clinical impression of lymphoreticular malignancy or metastatic disease
fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) was performed on the most prominent swellings
